comparator.name: Political Science
comparator.sourceNotes: The dated English curriculum totals sixty EC per year. International Relations is retained using the first-listed specialisation on the primary programme page. The twelve-credit core module, six-credit sustainability elective, eighteen seminar credits, twelve-credit thesis project and thirty open credits form one route; other specialisations are not added to its total.

components.name: History of Europe and the modern world since 1750
Academic skills for political scientists I
Academic skills for political scientists II
Academic skills for political scientists III
Research methods
components.note: Research Methods requires at least 42 first-year EC, including Introduction to Political Science Research. The later research project requires Research Methods; this pathway completes it first.

components.name: Research project II: Practicing research skills
Core module - International relations
components.note: The International Relations core module requires at least 42 first-year EC. This example retains the specialisation selected from the primary programme page before UCR construction.

components.name: Sustainability politics. Perspectives and debates
components.note: This example selects Sustainability Politics: Perspectives and Debates, 6 EC. It requires at least 42 first-year EC and cannot be combined with the alternative Violence and Security or European Union Politics module.

components.name: Beyond the headlines
components.note: Beyond the Headlines is an eligible 6 EC seminar in the International Relations route. The 2026–2027 offering examines American politics and its international connections. Entry requires the full first year and at least 42 year-2 EC.

components.name: Democratic Backsliding
components.note: Democratic Backsliding is an eligible 12 EC seminar in the International Relations route. Entry requires the full first year and at least 42 year-2 EC; prior Democracies, Autocracies and Transitions is recommended.

components.name: Contesting the Liberal International Order
components.note: The selected 12 EC thesis project is Contesting the Liberal International Order. Entry requires the full first year and at least 42 year-2 EC, including Research Methods. Completing both prior years meets the condition. The selected seminars and thesis are offered in the first semester; thirty EC remain open afterward.

components.name: Free-choice electives: Optional subjects
components.note: Thirty EC remain open for approved elective or minor study within or outside Political Science, exchange or an optional placement. No particular minor, placement host or elective is assumed.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The generic bachelor has five official core-module specialisations and none is identified as the broad default. alternativeSelection.assessment: A broad political-institutions response is the closest option. International conflict/governance and policy/political economy are separately evidenced priorities with concrete curricular consequences. comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both examine government policy in relation to economic organisation and distribution. UvA also studies the history and institutional foundations of capitalism and political-economic theory; UCR concentrates on public intervention and spending.
Both develop research design, evidence evaluation, measurement and empirical analysis. UCR includes a student research project in a broader disciplinary setting.
Both examine sustainability transitions through power, institutions, inclusion, collective action and governance frameworks.
Both study the historical development of modern political, economic and social systems. UCR starts in 1815 rather than 1750.
Both develop an independent academic research question, source work and a substantial scholarly paper. UCR uses historical rather than specifically political-science inquiry.
Both examine constitutional and administrative institutions, rights and legal constraints on public power. UvA situates these in an integrated law-and-politics introduction.
Both examine the history of political ideas through primary texts and relate them to political problems.
Both compare democratic and authoritarian institutions, transitions, political actors and explanations of regime change.
Both develop international-relations theories and apply them to global political problems.
Both develop a political research design, collect or code evidence and analyse and communicate findings. UCR uses an EU parliamentary project; UvA offers broader supervised research themes.
Both examine public policy, actors, policy processes and frameworks for analysing collective responses to social problems.

Both examine international power, conflict, colonial legacies, inequality and security. UvA is a broader advanced survey of International Relations; UCR concentrates on conflict and peace through several disciplines.
Both develop empirical inquiry and methodological judgement. UCR specialises in qualitative methods; UvA also includes quantitative and inferential statistical methods.
Both analyse power, inequality, social categories and difference through competing theoretical perspectives. UvA gives a specifically political and intersectional focus.

notes.text: UvA provides a dedicated Political Science sequence with a chosen core module, advanced seminars, integrated research training and a required thesis. The UCR options combine substantial political study with law, history, social theory, economics and methods. audience.programmeDescription: Political Science at UvA studies power, institutions, political ideas, international relations and public policy through social-scientific research. Students complete a specialisation, advanced seminars and a thesis. This example uses International Relations.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR can combine substantial political study with history, law, social theory, economics and methods. Its options prioritise political institutions and social change, international conflict and governance, or policy and political economy. UvA provides a more integrated specialist and research sequence.
